purpose: Resolve binocular gaze geometry into monitor hypotheses and a safe policy before rendering.

activities.label: verify ray-plane resolution, uncertainty and static fallback

queries.question: Can binocular gaze be resolved against multiple physical monitor planes with explicit UNKNOWN states before any renderer is enabled?

assumptions: The input gaze vector is a synthetic estimator output, not camera ground truth.
Monitor axes define planar physical rectangles in world metres.
The eye midpoint is used as the ray origin for this first geometry contract.
A valid state is allowed to describe a region but not to mutate screen content.
kill_tests: Head translation with a fixed world target must preserve monitor UV.
Missing eyes, stale layouts, low confidence and invalid pose must return UNKNOWN.
Overlapping monitor hypotheses must return ambiguous_monitor.
Mouse and keyboard context must never become gaze ground truth.
The geometry probe must not open a camera or mutate display content.
unknowns: Accuracy and latency of the real webcam/frontend on this machine.
Whether the monitor plane and eye centers can be estimated robustly in naturalistic motion.
What adaptive visual policy improves a human task without harming peripheral detection or comfort.
